sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Psychologists have always been interested in studying how we make sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 心理学家一直对研究我们如何理解世界充满兴趣。

sentences.en: Over and over, in many fields of research, one theme has recurred.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，在许多研究领域中，有一个主题不断重现。

sentences.en: What we see, hear, and feel is not just about what's in front of us.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到、听到和感受到的不仅仅取决于我们眼前的事物。

sentences.en: In the 1800s, early researchers began working in a branch of psychology called psychophysics.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，早期研究人员开始涉足心理学的一个分支，称为心理物理学。

sentences.en: It looked at how, for example, we can easily spot a single burning candle in a dark room.
sentences.zh: 它研究的是，例如，我们如何能轻易地在黑暗的房间里发现一支燃烧的蜡烛。

sentences.en: But put that same candle in a brightly lit room, and the flame can be hard to spot.
sentences.zh: 但如果把同一支蜡烛放在明亮的房间里，火焰就很难被发现了。

sentences.en: In other words, the context or frame around that burning candle matters.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这支燃烧的蜡烛周围的背景或框架很重要。

sentences.en: And that's true for many aspects of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这对我们生活中的许多方面来说都是如此。

sentences.en: If you break your foot the night before your wedding, you might feel very sorry for yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你在婚礼前夜摔断了脚，你可能会对自己的遭遇感到非常遗憾。

sentences.en: But if all you experience during a war is a broken foot, you would consider yourself extremely lucky.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在战争中经历的仅仅是摔断了一只脚，你就会觉得自己极其幸运。

sentences.en: Frames also shape how we think about our jobs.
sentences.zh: 框架也塑造了我们对工作的看法。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the second installment of our new series, Work 2.0.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将播出我们全新系列《工作 2.0》的第二部分。

sentences.en: Last week, we looked at how many organizations fail to notice the frictions that hold them back.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们探讨了许多组织如何未能察觉到阻碍它们发展的摩擦。

sentences.en: Today, we explore how smart companies and governments are reinventing the world of work by changing the frame around it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨精明的公司和政府如何通过改变工作周围的框架来重塑工作世界。

sentences.en: The world of work and the world of play are different worlds.
sentences.zh: 工作世界和娱乐世界是两个不同的世界。

sentences.en: At least, they seem that way.
sentences.zh: 至少，它们看起来是这样的。

sentences.en: When we are at work, we are supposed to be serious.
sentences.zh: 当我们工作时，我们应该表现得严肃。

sentences.en: Play is the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 娱乐则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: We play games to relax, to kick back with friends, to have fun.
sentences.zh: 我们玩游戏是为了放松，为了和朋友一起消遣，为了获得乐趣。

sentences.en: At the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School, Ethan Malik asks if these worlds have more in common than we think,
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院，伊桑·莫利克提出了这样一个问题：这两个世界的共同点是否比我们想象的要多，

sentences.en: and whether the world of work has a lot to learn from the psychology of games.
sentences.zh: 以及工作世界是否有很多东西可以从游戏心理学中学习。

sentences.en: Ethan Malik, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 伊桑·莫利克，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I want to start by talking about the ubiquity of games in our lives, Ethan.
sentences.zh: 伊桑，我想先谈谈游戏在我们生活中的无处不在。

sentences.en: You know, social scientists are always talking about, you know, what would happen if a, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，社会科学家总是在谈论，你知道，如果一个，你知道的，

sentences.en: a hypothetical anthropologist from Mars would pay a visit to planet Earth.
sentences.zh: 一个来自火星的假设性人类学家访问地球会发生什么。

sentences.en: And surely a visitor from another planet would notice how integral games are to human life, starting right from childhood.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，来自另一个星球的访客会注意到游戏对人类生活有多么重要，而且这种重要性从童年就开始了。

sentences.en: It's actually quite remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这其实相当引人注目。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, we are a game-playing people.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我们是一个爱玩游戏的民族。

sentences.en: That's a definition of humanity, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也是人性的一个定义。

sentences.en: So, we have evidence that we've played games through history, and obviously games are how we learn as a kid.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有证据表明我们在历史上一直在玩游戏，显而易见，游戏是我们小时候学习的方式。

sentences.en: Games are how we relax, how we compete with each other.
sentences.zh: 游戏是我们放松的方式，是我们互相竞争的方式。

sentences.en: So, it really is a ubiquitous feature of being human.
sentences.zh: 所以，它确实是人类的一个无处不在的特征。

sentences.en: And if you extend the world of gaming to include sports, we spend huge amounts of time not just playing recreational sports and watching sports,
sentences.zh: 如果你把游戏的世界延伸到包括体育运动在内，我们会花大量的时间，不仅是参加娱乐性体育运动和观看体育比赛，

sentences.en: but arguing about sports, dissecting it, engaging with it.
sentences.zh: 而且还在争论体育、剖析体育、参与体育。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is a thing we all care about.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都关心的事情。

sentences.en: We've cared about it for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我们已经关心了很久了。

sentences.en: There's actually graffiti in the Great Pyramids that suggests that there was actually game-playing among the various groups that were building the pyramids.
sentences.zh: 事实上，吉萨大金字塔里的涂鸦表明，建造金字塔的各个群体之间其实就已经存在游戏活动了。

sentences.en: The pyramids appear to have been built, at least in part, by drafted labor.
sentences.zh: 金字塔似乎至少有一部分是由征召的劳动力建造的。

sentences.en: And they would divide into teams with names like the Friends of Khufu or the Drunkards of Menkari and compete with each other to haul the most blocks and get beer as a reward for being the winner.
sentences.zh: 他们会分成不同的队伍，名字叫“胡夫的朋友”或“门卡拉的酒鬼”，通过互相竞争来搬运最多的石块，并以赢得啤酒作为奖励。

sentences.en: So, games have been with us as a motivating factor for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，游戏作为一种激励因素陪伴了我们很久很久。

sentences.en: Now, these days, Ethan, there's one type of game that dwarfs all the others, and those, of course, are video games.
sentences.zh: 如今，伊桑，有一种游戏让所有其他游戏都相形见绌，当然，那就是电子游戏。

sentences.en: Can you give me some sense of the scale of the popularity of video games?
sentences.zh: 你能让我对电子游戏受欢迎的规模有一个大致的了解吗？

sentences.en: I think one of my favorite stats is actually from a very popular game that you've probably heard of called Fortnite.
sentences.zh: 我想我最喜欢的数据之一其实来自于一个你可能听说过的非常流行的游戏，叫做《堡垒之夜》。

sentences.en: And at its peak of popularity during the pandemic last year, people played 3.2 billion hours of Fortnite in a single month.
sentences.zh: 在去年大流行期间其人气达到顶峰时，人们在一个月内就玩了32亿小时的《堡垒之夜》。

sentences.en: And just to put that in context, that's equivalent of building 29 Panama canals or 457 Empire State buildings.
sentences.zh: 为了做个对比，这相当于建造29条巴拿马运河或457栋帝国大厦。

sentences.en: Wait, you're saying the amount of time people spent playing Fortnite in one month, you could build 29 Panama canals or 457 Empire State buildings?
sentences.zh: 等等，你是说人们在一个月内玩《堡垒之夜》的时间，可以用来建造29条巴拿马运河或457栋帝国大厦？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you could get the people to work.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让这些人去工作的话。

sentences.en: A lot of them are middle schoolers, so it probably wouldn't be legal, but yes.
sentences.zh: 他们当中很多是初中生，所以可能不太合法，但是是的。

sentences.en: Well, that's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: I mean, you've also cited a survey that once asked people in three Canadian cities to identify a photo of the prime minister of Canada
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你还引用过一个调查，该调查曾要求加拿大三个城市的居民辨认一张加拿大总理的照片，

sentences.en: and a photo of a character from a famous Nintendo video game.
sentences.zh: 以及一张著名任天堂电子游戏角色的照片。

sentences.en: What did the survey find, Ethan?
sentences.zh: 调查结果是什么，伊桑？

sentences.en: Oh, far more people were able to identify Mario than Stephen Harper, who was the prime minister at the time.
sentences.zh: 哦，能够认出马里奥的人比认出时任总理斯蒂芬·哈珀的人多得多。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't that astonishing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这难道不令人震惊吗？

sentences.en: I mean, people are recognizing a fictional Italian plumber in a game versus the prime minister of their own country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们竟然能认出一个游戏里的虚构意大利水管工，却认不出自己国家的总理。

sentences.en: I don't think it's that surprising because of our level of engagement.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并没有那么令人惊讶，因为我们的参与度很高。

sentences.en: Just like if you ask people to remember the circle of people they knew in high school,
sentences.zh: 就像如果你让人们回忆他们在高中时认识的人的圈子，

sentences.en: they might have more trouble than remembering who was on their local sports team during that same period.
sentences.zh: 他们可能比回忆在同一时期谁加入了他们当地的运动队还要困难。

sentences.en: We really connect to games as people.
sentences.zh: 作为人，我们真的与游戏有着紧密的联系。

sentences.en: Now, this may be hard for people who don't play video games to understand, but the business of video games dwarfs many other industries.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于不玩电子游戏的人来说，这可能很难理解，但电子游戏产业让许多其他行业相形见绌。

sentences.en: Can you give me a sense of the scale, the business of the video gaming industry?
sentences.zh: 你能让我感受一下这个规模吗，电子游戏产业的规模？

sentences.en: It's bigger than movies.
sentences.zh: 它比电影还要大。

sentences.en: It's bigger than music.
sentences.zh: 它比音乐还要大。

sentences.en: It is the biggest entertainment industry by far, and its influence is everywhere, right?
sentences.zh: 它是迄今为止最大的娱乐产业，其影响力无处不在，对吧？

sentences.en: It drives the adoption of new technologies, whether it's virtual reality or the Apple App Store.
sentences.zh: 它推动了新技术的采用，无论是虚拟现实还是苹果应用商店。

sentences.en: It's an amazingly ubiquitous part of what we do, and the money flowing into it is huge.
sentences.zh: 它是我们所做事情中一个惊人且无处不在的部分，流入其中的资金是巨大的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I want to contrast what we've just heard about the world of games with the world of work.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在想把我们刚才听到的关于游戏世界的内容与工作世界进行对比。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the TV show Friends, where the character Rachel expresses how many people feel about the world of work.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段电视剧《老友记》里的片段，角色瑞秋在其中表达了许多人对工作世界的感受。

sentences.en: Oh, God, I hate my job.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，我讨厌我的工作。

sentences.en: I hate it.
sentences.zh: 我恨死它了。

sentences.en: I hate my job.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌我的工作。

sentences.en: I hate it.
sentences.zh: 我恨死它了。

sentences.en: Oh, no, honey, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，亲爱的，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Oh, I want to quit, but then I think I should stick it out.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想辞职，但转念一想，我又觉得我应该坚持下去。

sentences.en: Then I think, why would such a person stay in such a demeaning job just because it's remotely related to the field they're interested in?
sentences.zh: 然后我想，为什么这样一个人会仅仅因为一份工作跟她感兴趣的领域有一点点关系，就留在一份如此有辱人格的工作中呢？

sentences.en: Now, many, many people feel like Rachel, don't they, Ethan?
sentences.zh: 现在，许许多多的人都和瑞秋有同感，对吧，伊桑？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, work is full of frustrations and things that make it feel meaningless or a treadmill.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，工作充满了挫折，以及让人觉得毫无意义或像是无休止劳碌的事情。

sentences.en: And even if you're enjoying your job, I think everyone has times where they wonder, is this what I'm really doing with my life?
sentences.zh: 而且即使你很享受你的工作，我想每个人也都会有这样的时刻：他们会想，我这辈子到底在干什么？

sentences.en: I remember talking with the late anthropologist David Graeber some time ago, Ethan.
sentences.zh: 我记得不久前曾与已故人类学家大卫·格雷伯交谈过，伊桑。

sentences.en: He told me that vast numbers of people believe that jobs were not just boring, but pointless, that if their jobs disappeared tomorrow, no one would notice.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，绝大多数人认为工作不仅无聊，而且毫无意义，如果他们的工作明天消失了，根本不会有人注意到。

sentences.en: And it sounded like a terribly sad commentary on what work feels like for many people.
sentences.zh: 听起来，对于许多人来说，这像是对工作感受的一种极其悲哀的评论。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that many people don't feel meaning in their work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为许多人在工作中感受不到意义。

sentences.en: They don't feel a connection to a bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 他们感受不到与宏大图景的联系。

sentences.en: And that can be incredibly demotivating.
sentences.zh: 这可能会极大地消磨人的积极性。

sentences.en: Now, the life of a Wharton school professor sounds very exciting,
sentences.zh: 现在，沃顿商学院教授的生活听起来非常令人兴奋，

sentences.en: but surely you must have some points in your life when you feel like your own life is marked by drudgery and boredom and repetition?
sentences.zh: 但你肯定也有过这样的时刻：你觉得自己的生活充斥着苦差事、无聊和重复？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对有。

sentences.en: I mean, just like anyone else, I had had a series of jobs before becoming a professor that were quite tedious,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像其他人一样，在成为教授之前我也做过一系列相当沉闷的工作，

sentences.en: ranging from sorting broken computer equipment to cleaning up parking lots at shopping centers.
sentences.zh: 从分类损坏的电脑设备到清理购物中心的停车场。

sentences.en: So this was before we had, you know, podcasts, right?
sentences.zh: 所以那是在我们有，你知道的，播客之前的时代，对吧？

sentences.en: So it was just the radio you were listening to.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时只能听收音机。

sentences.en: And it was both gross and boring.
sentences.zh: 既恶心又无聊。

sentences.en: So you'd start to turn work into a game.
sentences.zh: 所以你会开始把工作变成一场游戏。

sentences.en: So I was, how many cigarette butts can I get in my scoop before I have to empty it out?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时会想：在我必须倒掉垃圾之前，我的铲子里能铲进去多少个烟头？

sentences.en: Can I get one of each kind of garbage before this song is over?
sentences.zh: 在这首歌放完之前，我能不能每种垃圾都捡到一个？

sentences.en: So, you know, making up games and challenges that turn this boring work into something at least somewhat more interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，编造一些游戏和挑战，把这无聊的工作变得至少稍微有趣一点。

sentences.en: Well, as much as I'd like to say being a professor is unending excitement, there are aspects of the job,
sentences.zh: 好吧，尽管我很想说当教授充满了无尽的刺激，但工作中确实也有一些方面，

sentences.en: whether that's cleaning giant data sets or sitting through some of the particularly long meetings that we sometimes have in some committees,
sentences.zh: 无论是清理庞大的数据集，还是参加我们在某些委员会中有时要开的那些特别漫长的会议，

sentences.en: though I probably shouldn't admit that on podcasts, but that can feel a bit tedious, yes.
sentences.zh: 虽然我可能不该在播客里承认这一点，但那确实会让人觉得有点沉闷，是的。

sentences.en: So, Ethan, we've looked at how, you know, many people love games and fun and many people think of work as being, you know, drudgery or repetition.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊桑，我们已经看到了，你知道的，许多人喜欢游戏和快乐，而许多人则认为工作是，你知道的，苦差事或重复劳动。

sentences.en: But again, looking from the perspective of that anthropologist from Mars, there's a paradox here, which is many dimensions of games look a lot like work.
sentences.zh: 但同样，从那个火星人类学家的视角来看，这里存在一个悖论，那就是游戏的许多维度看起来非常像工作。

sentences.en: Talk to me about The SiMs.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊《模拟人生》吧。

sentences.en: So The Sims is an incredibly popular sort of life simulator.
sentences.zh: 所以《模拟人生》是一种非常受欢迎的生活模拟器。

sentences.en: So you build families, you build houses, you have people live in these houses and kind of go through their daily jobs.
sentences.zh: 你建立家庭，建造房屋，让人们住在这些房子里，并经历他们日常的工作。

sentences.en: And people use this for all sorts of reasons, sort of a living dollhouse.
sentences.zh: 人们出于各种原因使用它，把它当成一个活生生的娃娃屋。

sentences.en: But what always amazes me about The Sims is how much time people are willing to spend just setting things up kind of correctly.
sentences.zh: 但《模拟人生》最让我惊叹的是，人们愿意花多少时间把事情安排得恰到好处。

sentences.en: So, for example, people have recreated the entire IKEA catalog, including historical IKEA chairs,
sentences.zh: 例如，人们重现了整个宜家产品目录，包括历史上的宜家椅子，

sentences.en: so you can decorate your house exactly the way you would your dorm or your other home.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以完全按照你对宿舍或其他家里的设想来装饰你的房子。

sentences.en: And it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: People spend hours just getting haircuts right.
sentences.zh: 人们花上几个小时只为了把发型弄对。

sentences.en: So, you know, the kinds of things that we do on a regular basis in our daily lives, people are happy to recreate in these virtual worlds as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们在日常生活中定期做的那类事情，人们也很乐意在这些虚拟世界中重新创造出来。

sentences.en: But isn't it interesting that in our daily lives, these often feel like chores.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在我们的日常生活中，这些往往感觉像是杂务。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you're telling your teenager to clean up her room or get her room in order, that feels like a chore.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果你让你的青少年女儿打扫房间或把房间收拾好，那感觉就像是一项苦差事。

sentences.en: But to design a room on a virtual game sounds like fun.
sentences.zh: 但在虚拟游戏中设计一个房间听起来却很有趣。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that is the sort of paradox at the heart of trying to connect games and work, right, is that work is often tedious.
sentences.zh: 这就是试图将游戏和工作联系起来的核心悖论，对吧，那就是工作往往是单调乏味的。

sentences.en: And the same thing in a game can be made to be terrific.
sentences.zh: 而游戏中的同一件事却可以做得非常棒。

sentences.en: I want to look at a few other dimensions of this paradox, Ethan.
sentences.zh: 我想看看这个悖论的其他几个维度，伊桑。

sentences.en: Games like, you know, Chutes and Ladders, and I don't know how many people play those anymore.
sentences.zh: 像这样的游戏，你知道的，比如《滑梯与梯子》，我不知道现在还有多少人在玩。

sentences.en: But there are many games where we routinely, you know, play the game for a while and then suddenly find ourselves back at square one.
sentences.zh: 但有很多游戏，我们经常，你知道的，玩了一会儿游戏，然后突然发现自己又回到了原点。

sentences.en: And now we have to, you know, march all the way back again, you know, to get back to where we were.
sentences.zh: 现在我们必须，你知道的，再次一路长途跋涉，你知道的，以便回到我们之前所在的地方。

sentences.en: So we constantly, in many aspects of games, have to deal with the kind of setbacks that in the real world, you know, strike us as really tedious.
sentences.zh: 所以在游戏的许多方面，我们必须不断应对那些在现实世界中，你知道的，让我们觉得非常沉闷的挫折。

sentences.en: Well, there's even a word for this in the game world, which is grind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在游戏界甚至有一个专门的词来形容这个，那就是“肝”（grind）。

sentences.en: So the idea of grinding is putting in tremendous amounts of work to advance your character or your game state to some degree.
sentences.zh: 所以“肝”的概念就是投入大量的工作来提升你的角色或你的游戏状态到某种程度。

sentences.en: And there's all kinds of games that include grind.
sentences.zh: 而且有各种各样的游戏都包含这种“肝”的机制。

sentences.en: You might spend 30 or 40 hours sometimes to just be able to get access to a particularly good-looking piece of equipment or to upgrade your skill in fishing in an online game.
sentences.zh: 有时你可能会花上30到40个小时，只为了能够获得一件特别好看的装备，或者在网络游戏中提升你的钓鱼技能。

sentences.en: So this sort of approach is really common.
sentences.zh: 所以这种方法真的很常见。

sentences.en: We see people being willing to go back to square one and start over again, over and over.
sentences.zh: 我们看到人们愿意回到原点，一遍又一遍地重新开始。

sentences.en: In fact, some of my favorite games are these type of games called roguelikes, where the whole idea is you keep failing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我最喜欢的一些游戏是被称为“Roguelike”的这类游戏，其核心理念就是你不断地失败。

sentences.en: You might fail hundreds of times before you succeed once or twice.
sentences.zh: 你可能会失败几百次，然后才能成功一两次。

sentences.en: And it's one of my favorite categories.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的类别之一。

sentences.en: I find that there's something, you know, failure in the real world is really difficult and painful.
sentences.zh: 我发现有些东西，你知道的，现实世界中的失败非常困难且痛苦。

sentences.en: And failure in games can kind of be a sort of release where you get to try again and try and be more perfect the next time around.
sentences.zh: 而在游戏中的失败可以算是一种释放，你可以再次尝试，并在下一次争取表现得更加完美。

sentences.en: Now, I mentioned David Graeber's research a second ago into how many people find their work to be pointless.
sentences.zh: 刚才我提到了大卫·格雷伯关于许多人觉得他们的工作毫无意义的研究。

sentences.en: So this is another dimension of the paradox, because almost by definition, games are pointless.
sentences.zh: 所以这是该悖论的另一个维度，因为几乎根据定义，游戏就是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: You know, whether you end up with more green cones than red cones or kill the pink dragon or manage to land the ball inside the line,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，无论你最后得到的绿锥体多于红锥体，还是杀死了粉红色的龙，或者设法把球打进线内，

sentences.en: if you apply the same logic that people bring to their work, you can say, you know, who cares?
sentences.zh: 如果你把人们带到工作中的那种逻辑应用到这里，你就可以说，你知道的，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: It's pointless.
sentences.zh: 这毫无意义。

sentences.en: Yet somehow when it comes to games, this pointlessness is somehow appealing instead of demoralizing.
sentences.zh: 然而不知何故，当谈到游戏时，这种无意义感不仅没有让人士气低落，反而颇具吸引力。

sentences.en: No one ever says, OK, I captured the flag.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人会说：“好吧，我夺取了旗帜。”

sentences.en: Who cares?
sentences.zh: “谁在乎呢？”

sentences.en: It's pointless.
sentences.zh: “这毫无意义。”

sentences.en: Yeah, we have a category in our heads of sort of feelings of accomplishment we get from games are real, even if the experience isn't.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们脑海里有一种分类，即我们从游戏中获得的成就感是真实的，即使这种体验本身不是。

sentences.en: So I think you're highlighting really nicely this kind of contrast between the fact that our real life experiences,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你很好地突出了这种对比，即我们的现实生活体验，

sentences.en: even though they actually matter in the world, often don't feel like there's a point.
sentences.zh: 虽然它们在现实世界中真的很重要，但通常让人觉得毫无意义。

sentences.en: Well, the things where we know they don't matter in the world, we get satisfaction out of them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于那些我们知道在现实世界中无关紧要的事情，我们却能从中获得满足感。

sentences.en: And I think that that is one of the most interesting aspects of games.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是游戏最有趣的方面之一。

sentences.en: So we've looked at how games often involve similar kinds of repetition and setbacks and drudgery that lots of people experience at work.
sentences.zh: 我们之前探讨过，游戏通常包含许多人在工作中经历的同类重复、挫折和苦差事。

sentences.en: There is another aspect of games that also looks a lot like work.
sentences.zh: 游戏的另一个方面也与工作非常相似。

sentences.en: Games often demand intense effort.
sentences.zh: 游戏往往需要付出极大的努力。

sentences.en: Now, some of the earliest games we learned to play as children involve, you know, physical activity, running.
sentences.zh: 我们小时候最早学会的一些游戏，包含体力活动，比如跑步。

sentences.en: And many of us continue to pursue these activities into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人成年后仍在继续进行这些活动。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the 2019 Boston Marathon, where the commentators are talking about an athlete approaching the finish line after running more than 26 miles.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段2019年波士顿马拉松的录音，解说员在片中谈到了一名运动员跑完26多英里后接近终点的情景。

sentences.en: What a finish to see that.
sentences.zh: 看到这样的冲刺真是一个精彩的结局。

sentences.en: I mean, you could just see going to everything, arms, legs, and everything is shot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能看出他拼尽了全力，胳膊、腿以及整个身体都透支了。

sentences.en: So painful.
sentences.zh: 太痛苦了。

sentences.en: I kind of feared for Desisa that he might rip his hamstring muscles.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有点担心德西萨会拉伤腿筋。

sentences.en: He was straining so hard at the finish.
sentences.zh: 他在冲刺时紧绷到了极点。

sentences.en: I mean, surely, Ethan, you know, the anthropologists from Mars would say, you know, these kinds of activities don't look like fun.
sentences.zh: 伊森，我觉得火星来的人类学家肯定会说，这类活动看起来一点也不好玩。

sentences.en: And yet, tens of thousands of people voluntarily sign up to do them over and over again and think of these activities as being, you know,
sentences.zh: 然而，数以万计的人却自愿一次又一次地报名参加，并认为这些活动是

sentences.en: some of the most meaningful achievements in their life.
sentences.zh: 他们一生中最有意义的成就之一。

sentences.en: I think it goes back to what you discussed earlier, which is that, you know, meaning in our work is about how we feel about this, right?
sentences.zh: 我想这可以追溯到你刚才讨论的话题，也就是我们在工作中的意义其实取决于我们的感受，对吧？

sentences.en: And when we play games, there's some degree of we get to pick the competition that we're in.
sentences.zh: 而当我们玩游戏时，我们在某种程度上可以挑选自己参与的竞赛。

sentences.en: And we pick competitions that are meaningful for us.
sentences.zh: 我们挑选对我们有意义的竞赛。

sentences.en: And there is this sense of accomplishment and joy that comes with achieving goals that you set for yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 实现自己设定的目标会带来一种成就感和喜悦感，对吧？

sentences.en: Even if those goals might seem meaningless to the outside world.
sentences.zh: 即使这些目标对外面的世界来说可能显得毫无意义。

sentences.en: I mean, do you do this yourself, Ethan?
sentences.zh: 伊森，你自己会这样做吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do you do this when you're working out, for example, or when you're, I don't know if you're a runner or a swimmer.
sentences.zh: 比如你在锻炼时，或者我不知道你是否是个跑步或游泳爱好者，你会这样做吗？

sentences.en: Do you sort of set artificial targets for yourself and derive inordinate pleasure when you meet those targets?
sentences.zh: 你会不会给自己设定一些人为的目标，并在达成这些目标时获得无与伦比的快乐？

sentences.en: Well, I have those targets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实有这些目标。

sentences.en: I'm a big Apple Watch workout user.
sentences.zh: 我是苹果手表锻炼功能的大力支持者。

sentences.en: But there's another dimension that I think you've hinted at throughout our conversation so far, which is a lot of this involves other people, right?
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个维度，我觉得你在我们刚才的对话中已经暗示过了，那就是这其中很大一部分涉及到其他人，对吧？

sentences.en: Whether that's sports or marathon running, you want to beat someone else.
sentences.zh: 无论是体育运动还是马拉松跑步，你都想战胜别人。

sentences.en: So for me, it's one of my sisters and I, since the pandemic, have been competing weekly for exercise on the Apple Watch.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，自大流行以来，我和我的一个姐姐每周都会在苹果手表上进行锻炼比赛。

sentences.en: And I will keep an eye on it when she inevitably starts beating me.
sentences.zh: 当她不可避免地开始超越我时，我会密切关注。

sentences.en: I have gone downstairs to work out at 1130 at night to get those last 20 minutes in to try and overcome her point total,
sentences.zh: 我曾在夜里11点30分下楼锻炼，为了凑够最后20分钟，试图超越她的积分总和，

sentences.en: even though I think the score is currently like 44 weeks to five weeks or something like that, where she's won.
sentences.zh: 尽管目前的比分大概是她赢了44周对5周之类的悬殊差距。

sentences.en: But every time I pull it off, I feel great.
sentences.zh: 但每次我反败为胜时，我都感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's astonishing that people will exercise in order to have a metric on their watch or to beat somebody else instead of exercising to save their own lives.
sentences.zh: 是的，真让人惊讶，人们为了手表上的一个数据指标或者为了打败别人而锻炼，而不是为了拯救自己的生命而锻炼。

sentences.en: I mean, you would think that the latter would have more appeal.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得后者应该更有吸引力才对。

sentences.en: Except that, you know, saving our lives is a slow process and beating my sister is happening now.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，拯救我们的生命是一个缓慢的过程，而打败我姐姐是现在就能发生的。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a big difference between those.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这两者之间有很大的区别。

sentences.en: And that's a big problem with the work issue, too, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是工作问题中的一个大问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Your accomplishments are all for the future.
sentences.zh: 你的成就全部是为了未来。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you blow up an alien, you're blowing it up right now.
sentences.zh: 但是，当你炸毁一个外星人时，你是在当下就炸毁了它。

sentences.en: The world of play and the world of work have a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 游戏世界和工作世界有很多共同点。

sentences.en: They can both involve painstaking effort and repetitive tasks.
sentences.zh: 它们都可能包含煞费苦心的努力和重复性的任务。

sentences.en: Yet many people pay money to do one set of activities and resent doing the other, even though they get paid to do it.
sentences.zh: 然而，许多人花钱去做其中一套活动，却对另一套活动感到怨恨，尽管做后者还能拿到报酬。

sentences.en: When we come back, we uncover the psychology behind this paradox and what it tells us about how to make work more rewarding and perhaps even fun.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将揭开这种悖论背后的心理学，以及它如何启示我们让工作更有回报甚至更有趣。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹特。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹特。

sentences.en: Think back to when you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 回想一下你小时候的情景。

sentences.en: Ask yourself, did anyone have to force you to play games?
sentences.zh: 问问自己，有没有人强迫你玩游戏？

sentences.en: If you were like most kids, the answer is, of course not.
sentences.zh: 如果你像大多数孩子一样，答案当然是否定的。

sentences.en: Whether it was a game of tag or soccer or Minecraft, you often had to be torn away from games by your parents or teachers.
sentences.zh: 无论是玩抓人游戏、踢足球还是玩《我的世界》，你经常得让父母或老师把你强行拉开。

sentences.en: Think for a moment about how different that is from the world of what we call work.
sentences.zh: 花点时间想想，这与我们所谓的“工作”世界有多么不同。

sentences.en: Managers hovering over you, teachers yelling at you, people showering you with threats and inducements to stay on task.
sentences.zh: 经理对你虎视眈眈，老师对你大喊大叫，人们用各种威胁和诱惑来让你专注于任务。

sentences.en: At the Wharton School, Ethan Mollick teaches innovation and entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 在沃顿商学院，伊森·莫利克教授创新与创业学。

sentences.en: He studies why games have a radically different effect on our minds than work.
sentences.zh: 他研究为什么游戏对我们大脑的影响与工作有着根本的不同。

sentences.en: Ethan, we talked about how many games aren't all that different from jobs in that they can also involve repetitive, boring, or difficult activities.
sentences.zh: 伊森，我们讨论过许多游戏与工作并没有太大区别，因为它们也可能包含重复、枯燥或困难的活动。

sentences.en: But there are many psychological differences between work and play.
sentences.zh: 但工作与游戏之间存在着许多心理差异。

sentences.en: And one of them has to do with the way games often incorporate stories.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就与游戏融入故事的方式有关。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how games use storytelling to hold our interest?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我游戏是如何通过讲故事来吸引我们的兴趣的吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So our lives at work often don't fit a neat narrative, right?
sentences.zh: 我们在工作中的生活往往不符合一个清晰的叙事，对吧？

sentences.en: We're not hero.
sentences.zh: 我们不是英雄。

sentences.en: We're not villain.
sentences.zh: 我们不是恶棍。

sentences.en: There's not a story of progression.
sentences.zh: 这里没有一个发展的故事。

sentences.en: We have to do that for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这一切都得靠我们自己去完成。

sentences.en: But humans are kind of narrative machines.
sentences.zh: 但人类可以说是叙事机器。

sentences.en: We've always told stories.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讲述故事。

sentences.en: And games are great because they give you a context or a meaning for your work in that storyline.
sentences.zh: 游戏之所以棒，是因为它们为你在该故事情节中的工作提供了一个语境或意义。

sentences.en: You're not just clicking a button.
sentences.zh: 你不仅仅是在点击一个按钮。

sentences.en: You're saving a planet.
sentences.zh: 你是在拯救一个星球。

sentences.en: You're not just moving a mouse and completing some task.
sentences.zh: 你不仅仅是在移动鼠标完成某些任务。

sentences.en: You are helping your team win.
sentences.zh: 你是在帮助你的团队赢得胜利。

sentences.en: So there's both a sort of small-scale story that we feel like we're part of that narrative and also the larger-scale stories.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里既有一种我们觉得身处其中的小规模叙事，也有更宏大的故事。

sentences.en: Many games are built around storyline, right?
sentences.zh: 许多游戏都是围绕故事情节构建的，对吧？

sentences.en: That you are accomplishing some goal.
sentences.zh: 即你在达成某种目标。

sentences.en: You're often the hero of the tale, saving the world or improving something in some way.
sentences.zh: 你通常是故事中的英雄，拯救世界或以某种方式改善现状。

sentences.en: And that's a really powerful tool because we can imagine ourselves in those positions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常强大的工具，因为我们可以把自己代入这些角色中。

sentences.en: And that makes our choices feel meaningful.
sentences.zh: 这让我们做出的选择显得很有意义。

sentences.en: The connection that you're drawing here might explain why movies lend themselves to games and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 你在这里建立的联系或许可以解释为什么电影很容易改编成游戏，反之亦然。

sentences.en: Like the Harry Potter movie franchise has spawned dozens of games, right?
sentences.zh: 就像《哈利·波特》系列电影衍生出了几十款游戏一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, one step beyond the movie is being in the movie, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，比看电影更进一步的就是身处电影之中，对吧？

sentences.en: So even though movie games have a reputation for being pretty mediocre games, they're also continuously popular.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管电影改编游戏素来名声一般，觉得它们相当平庸，但它们依然持续受欢迎。

sentences.en: Not because the gameplay is amazing, but because you want to be Harry Potter or Rey or Luke Skywalker or whoever you want to inhabit.
sentences.zh: 不是因为游戏玩法有多惊艳，而是因为你想成为哈利·波特、雷伊、卢克·天行者或任何你想扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Something you said a moment ago really struck me, which is it's not just that games have stories,
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的一句话真的触动了我，那就是游戏不仅有故事，

sentences.en: but sometimes the reward for playing a game is that you unlock new elements of the story.
sentences.zh: 而且有时玩游戏的奖励是你解锁了故事的新元素。

sentences.en: So playing the game becomes a way to move forward in the narrative.
sentences.zh: 因此，玩游戏成了一种推动叙事发展的方式。

sentences.en: Can you give me an example of a game that works like this?
sentences.zh: 你能举出一个这样运作的游戏的例子吗？

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of games depend on sort of a cliffhanger or next event.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多游戏都依赖于某种悬念或接下来的事件。

sentences.en: And the feeling of you're gaining power, gaining control is really important.
sentences.zh: 那种获得力量、获得掌控感的感觉非常重要。

sentences.en: So there's classic role-playing games where there's the Final Fantasy games or The Witcher, where the story is compelling.
sentences.zh: 比如经典的RPG角色扮演游戏，像《最终幻想》或《巫师》，它们的故事引人入胜。

sentences.en: You want to find out what happens next and your choices affect the world around you.
sentences.zh: 你想知道接下来会发生什么，你的选择会影响你周围的世界。

sentences.en: Got a minute?
sentences.zh: 有空吗？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I'm looking for a woman.
sentences.zh: 我在找一个女人。

sentences.en: Long hair, dressed in black and white.
sentences.zh: 长头发，穿着黑白相间的衣服。

sentences.en: Seen anyone like that?
sentences.zh: 见过这样的人吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I actually still have some games that I played, one called Mass Effect, that I still, you know, about six years later,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我仍然保留着一些我玩过的游戏，有一款叫《质量效应》，大约六年过去了，我仍然，

sentences.en: think about how I made a bad choice that doomed one of my companions in the game and still regret it at this point.
sentences.zh: 会想起我当时做出过一个糟糕的选择，导致游戏中的一个同伴送命，至今仍感到后悔。

sentences.en: I should have loaded that saved game.
sentences.zh: 我当时真该读取那个存档的。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, Jack.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，杰克。

sentences.en: So games allow us to follow narratives and become entranced by stories, but they also do something else that you hinted at a moment ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，游戏让我们能够跟随叙事并被故事吸引，但它们还做了一件你刚才暗示过的事情。

sentences.en: They offer us a chance to try things out and to take chances.
sentences.zh: 它们为我们提供了尝试新事物和承担风险的机会。

sentences.en: So, in other words, when you let down the character Jack in the game, that was painful, but presumably not as painful as letting Jack down in real life.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你在游戏中让角色杰克失望时，那确实很痛苦，但想必没有在现实生活中让杰克失望那么痛苦。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how games allow us to simulate life, but with lower stakes?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈游戏是如何让我们在低风险的情况下模拟生活的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so we are drawn to systems, and we like to be able to kind of play with systems, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们会被系统吸引，我们喜欢能够摆弄系统，对吧？

sentences.en: Failure is interesting, and it's why flight simulators are interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 失败很有趣，这也是飞行模拟器有趣的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: The chance to fail, to learn from mistakes, and to try again is an exciting thing to do, right?
sentences.zh: 有机会经历失败、从错误中吸取教训并再次尝试，是一件令人兴奋的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Building sandcastles is fun.
sentences.zh: 堆沙堡很有趣。

sentences.en: Knocking them over is actually more fun, right?
sentences.zh: 推倒它们其实更有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: The sort of destruction, the playing with reality is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 那种破坏的快感、与现实玩耍的感觉非常有趣。

sentences.en: So games lend themselves very naturally to thinking about systems and how they break and how they fail,
sentences.zh: 因此，游戏非常自然地引导我们去思考系统以及它们是如何崩溃和失败的，

sentences.en: and then you get the real sense of improvement from that failure in games that you don't in real life, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你在游戏中从这种失败中获得的真实提升感，是现实生活中没有的，对吧？

sentences.en: If your startup company fails, that feels pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 如果你的初创公司失败了，感觉会相当糟糕。

sentences.en: But if it fails in a game, maybe that was interesting, and now you're going to do something different next time.
sentences.zh: 但如果它在游戏中失败了，也许这还挺有意思的，接下来你就可以尝试做点不一样的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you get killed in a game, you start over.
sentences.zh: 所以如果在游戏中丧命，你可以重头再来。

sentences.en: If you lose a match, you come back and play again tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果你输了一场比赛，你可以卷土重来，明天再玩。

sentences.en: You mess up at work, you could get fired.
sentences.zh: 如果你在工作中搞砸了，你可能会被炒鱿鱼。

sentences.en: Exactly, and that makes us less willing to take the risks that are both important for, you know, learning in work.
sentences.zh: 正是如此，这让我们更不愿去承担那些对工作中的学习同样重要的风险。

sentences.en: Like, we learn from failure, but we're very afraid to fail.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们从失败中学习，但我们又非常害怕失败。

sentences.en: And even if we fail, we're afraid to publicly discuss our failure, right?
sentences.zh: 而且即使我们失败了，我们也害怕公开讨论我们的失败，对吧？

sentences.en: Because then people might think we're not competent.
sentences.zh: 因为那样别人可能会认为我们能力不足。

sentences.en: So all of that holds back our advancement in the world of work.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都阻碍了我们在工作世界中的晋升。

sentences.en: But in games, failure is interesting.
sentences.zh: 但在游戏中，失败很有趣。

sentences.en: Talking about failure is interesting.
sentences.zh: 谈论失败也很有趣。

sentences.en: People make YouTube videos of the biggest disasters they had in games.
sentences.zh: 人们会把他们在游戏中遇到的最大灾难剪辑成YouTube视频。

sentences.en: So it's a very different attitude towards the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种截然不同的世界态度。

sentences.en: You know, I spoke some time ago with your fellow University of Pennsylvania researcher, Paul Rosen,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不久前我采访了你的宾夕法尼亚大学研究员同事保罗·罗森，

sentences.en: and he explained this concept to me called benign masochism.
sentences.zh: 他向我解释了一个概念，叫做良性受虐。

sentences.en: When you go bungee jumping or ride a roller coaster, you have an illusion of danger or pain without actual danger or pain.
sentences.zh: 当你去蹦极或坐过山车时，你体验到的是没有真正危险或痛苦的危险或痛苦幻觉。

sentences.en: And in some ways, games allow us to taste what it feels like to be attacked or under siege or even killed
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，游戏让我们无需承担这些事情带来的现实风险，就能体会被攻击、遭围困甚至被杀害的感觉。

sentences.en: without the real risks attendant to those things.
sentences.zh: 正是如此，对这些事情感到好奇是很正常的。

sentences.en: Exactly, and it's normal to sort of be curious about these things.
sentences.zh: 我其实曾经去过一个军事游戏训练大会，我只是对所有游戏的失败状态很好奇。

sentences.en: I actually once went to a military game training convention, and I was kind of just curious about the failure states for all the games.
sentences.zh: 所以我试玩了每一个模拟器，这些可都是价值数百万美元的模拟器，

sentences.en: So I would play every simulator, and these were multi-million dollar simulators,
sentences.zh: 看看把坦克开下悬崖或者把飞机撞毁时会发生什么。

sentences.en: and see what happened when you drove the tank off a cliff or, you know, crashed the plane.
sentences.zh: 结果总是很无聊。

sentences.en: It was always boring.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实打破了一个坦克模拟器，因为我把它开撞到了墙上。

sentences.en: Although I did, I think, break one of the tank simulators by driving into a wall.
sentences.zh: 显然以前从来没人这么干过，结果把游戏给卡崩了。

sentences.en: And then apparently no one had ever done that before, and it broke the game.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们对这类情况下事情出错时会发生什么很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So, but I think we are interested in what happens when things go wrong in these kind of cases.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管其中有些东西看起来可能具有破坏性，但学习实际上就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and even though, of course, some of that might seem destructive, this is how learning actually happens.
sentences.zh: 当你打破某样东西时，你其实就对它的运作原理有了深刻的理解。

sentences.en: When you break something, you actually understand something deep about how it actually works.
sentences.zh: 从最基本的意义上讲，学习就是关于失败以及如何在下一次做得更好。

sentences.en: I mean, in the most basic sense, learning is about failure and about doing things better the next time.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么测试能帮助我们更好地学习。

sentences.en: It's why testing helps us learn better.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我现在的很多工作都是关于设计用于教学的游戏的原因。

sentences.en: It's why a lot of my work now is about designing games to teach,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我现在的很多工作都与设计寓教于乐的游戏有关，

sentences.en: because you can fail in a game and advance to the future, but if you fail in real life, it's costly, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你在游戏中失败了还可以进入下一个阶段，但在现实生活中失败代价高昂，对吧？

sentences.en: So this idea that we learn through failure, that we should experience more failure in our lives,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们通过失败来学习、我们应该在生活中经历更多失败这个想法，

sentences.en: is actually a really good one.
sentences.zh: 其实是一个非常棒的想法。

sentences.en: And there's this taunt in games as get good, right?
sentences.zh: 游戏中有一种嘲讽叫“变强（get good）”，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's something you could actually do in a game.
sentences.zh: 而这是你真能在游戏中做到的事。

sentences.en: You could practice and get good from failure.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过练习从失败中变强。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another dimension of the psychology of games.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈游戏心理学的另一个维度。

sentences.en: You know, if you like chess, maybe you've tried the game Play Magnus.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你喜欢国际象棋，你可能尝试过“Play Magnus”这款游戏。

sentences.en: It's named after the Norwegian chess star Magnus Carlsen.
sentences.zh: 它是以挪威国际象棋明星马格努斯·卡尔森的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And the conceit of the game is that you can play against Magnus Carlsen at 29 different skill levels,
sentences.zh: 这款游戏的构思是，你可以与不同技能水平的马格努斯·卡尔森进行29个级别的对战，

sentences.en: starting with playing with Magnus when he was age five and then age six and age seven.
sentences.zh: 从五岁时的马格努斯开始，然后是六岁、七岁。

sentences.en: And you can see at what point, you know, Magnus Carlsen starts to beat you.
sentences.zh: 你可以看看在哪个阶段，你知道的，马格努斯·卡尔森开始击败你。

sentences.en: Ethan, tell me how well-constructed games carefully find this balance
sentences.zh: 伊桑，请告诉我，设计精良的游戏是如何仔细把握这种平衡的：

sentences.en: between not running too far ahead of our abilities and not running too far behind our abilities.
sentences.zh: 既不让难度超出我们的能力太多，也不让难度落后我们的能力太多。

sentences.en: Well, you may have heard of the state of flow, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能听说过“心流（flow）”状态，对吧？

sentences.en: This famous psychological construct that that's when time vanishes at work, right?
sentences.zh: 这个著名的心理学概念，就是那种工作时时间飞逝的状态，对吧？

sentences.en: We get into a task and everything around us disappears.
sentences.zh: 我们全身心投入一项任务中，身边的所有东西都消失了。

sentences.en: Maybe we're working on a spreadsheet and everything's sort of focused down
sentences.zh: 也许我们在处理电子表格，所有注意力都集中下来，

sentences.en: and you looked up at hours had passed.
sentences.zh: 等你抬头时，几个小时已经过去了。

sentences.en: It's very commonly found in sports and activities.
sentences.zh: 这在体育运动和各种活动中非常常见。

sentences.en: And one of the keys to achieving that flow state is to neither be bored because the task is too easy
sentences.zh: 实现心流状态的关键之一，就是既不会因为任务太简单而感到无聊，

sentences.en: nor to be frustrated because the task is so hard.
sentences.zh: 也不会因为任务太难而感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And one of the things that a well-designed game does is it adjusts its difficulty level, right?
sentences.zh: 设计优秀的游戏所做的事情之一，就是调整它的难度级别，对吧？

sentences.en: You beat a level and then you get the next hardest level.
sentences.zh: 你通关了一个级别，就会迎来下一个最难的级别。

sentences.en: If you don't succeed, you play again until it becomes easy.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有成功，就再玩一次，直到它变得容易。

sentences.en: And the sense of accomplishment is something that you can get in a game
sentences.zh: 而这种成就感是你在游戏中可以获得的，

sentences.en: where everything is always calibrated to keep you in that flow state.
sentences.zh: 在游戏中，一切总是经过校准，让你保持在那种心流状态。

sentences.en: And it's not something we get to do in reality nearly as often.
sentences.zh: 而在现实中，我们几乎没有那么多机会体验到这一点。

sentences.en: So this reminds me of a concept sometimes called the Yerkes-Dodson Law,
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了一个有时被称为“耶基斯-多德森定律（Yerkes-Dodson Law）”的概念，

sentences.en: named after the psychologist Robert Yerkes and John Dodson.
sentences.zh: 它以心理学家罗伯特·耶基斯和约翰·多德森的名字命名。

sentences.en: They found that people's performance increases with mental arousal and with stress,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，随着心理唤醒度和压力的增加，人们的表现也会提高，

sentences.en: but only up to a certain point, beyond which stress becomes really detrimental.
sentences.zh: 但只能达到一定程度，超过这个程度后，压力就会变得非常有害。

sentences.en: Performance starts to decline.
sentences.zh: 表现开始下降。

sentences.en: I feel that good game designers are keenly aware of the Yerkes-Dodson Law.
sentences.zh: 我觉得优秀的游戏设计者对耶基斯-多德森定律有着敏锐的认识。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what the secret of games is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是游戏的秘诀所在。

sentences.en: If you look back to the earliest sort of video games and you think about Pac-Man or Mario Brothers or whatever it is,
sentences.zh: 如果你回看最早的那类电子游戏，想想《吃豆人》或《超级马里奥兄弟》之类的游戏，

sentences.en: levels start easy, right?
sentences.zh: 关卡都是从简单开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: And they get harder and harder until you lose.
sentences.zh: 它们变得越来越难，直到你输掉。

sentences.en: And, you know, then you play again, right?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，你就重新开始玩，对吧？

sentences.en: They're adjusting up to your difficulty level.
sentences.zh: 它们在根据你的难度水平进行调整。

sentences.en: You get a sense of mastery and accomplishment as you go forward.
sentences.zh: 随着你的前进，你会获得一种掌控感和成就感。

sentences.en: So games can adjust to difficulty.
sentences.zh: 所以游戏能够调整难度。

sentences.en: Work does not adjust to difficulty, right?
sentences.zh: 工作却不会调整难度，对吧？

sentences.en: In work, we just keep, you know, if our tasks are boring, it's likely to be boring for a while.
sentences.zh: 在工作中，我们只能，你知道的，如果我们的任务很无聊，它可能会无聊上一阵子。

sentences.en: If it's too stressful, we're stressed all the time.
sentences.zh: 如果压力太大，我们就会一直感到压力山大。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be great if work adjusted its difficulty level to keep us in the perfect level of engagement
sentences.zh: 如果工作能够调整其难度级别，让我们保持在完美的参与度水平，

sentences.en: without either being too stressed or getting bored?
sentences.zh: 既不会压力过大也不会感到无聊，那该有多好啊？

sentences.en: I want to talk about another dimension of games, which is that there, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈游戏的另一个维度，那就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: games often come with a clear set of rules.
sentences.zh: 游戏通常伴随着一套清晰的规则。

sentences.en: They give us clear feedback on where we are in the game, you know,
sentences.zh: 它们为我们在游戏中的位置提供清晰的反馈，你知道的，

sentences.en: what happens when we reach certain levels, how we can improve.
sentences.zh: 当我们达到某些级别时会发生什么，我们如何改进。

sentences.en: I mean, this is especially true in video games, but it's also true, you know, in sports.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在电子游戏中尤其如此，但在体育运动中也是如此。

sentences.en: We all agree that when a goal is scored, you know, you get a point.
sentences.zh: 我们都同意，当一个球进门时，你知道的，你就会得一分。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether the clarity of the rules of games, you know, even if they're artificial,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，游戏规则的清晰性，你知道的，即使它们是人为设定的，

sentences.en: allow us to engage in games without the ambiguity that often comes into play in work settings
sentences.zh: 是否能让我们参与游戏，而没有工作环境中经常出现的那种含糊不清，

sentences.en: where you don't always know what the rules are or how to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 在工作中，你并不总是知道规则是什么，或者如何脱颖而出。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So there's clarity.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有清晰度。

sentences.en: We know what we're supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 我们知道自己该做什么。

sentences.en: Even with the uncertainties are, you know, in a puzzle game, right?
sentences.zh: 即使存在不确定性，你知道的，在益智游戏中，对吧？

sentences.en: You may not know the exact answer, but you know there's an answer for you.
sentences.zh: 你可能不知道确切的答案，但你知道为你准备了一个答案。

sentences.en: The second interesting thing about games is this concept that people study games call the magic circle,
sentences.zh: 关于游戏的第二个有趣之处，是游戏研究人员称之为“魔圈（magic circle）”的概念，

sentences.en: which is when people play games, they enter the magic circle.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们在玩游戏时，会进入这个魔圈。

sentences.en: They agree to be bound by the rules of the game.
sentences.zh: 他们同意受游戏规则的约束。

sentences.en: That's why no matter how frustrating that monopoly game is, you don't break the rules and start to cheat, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么无论那局《大富翁》多么令人沮丧，你都不会打破规则开始作弊，对吧？

sentences.en: We feel like there's stakes there and we feel bound to work with each other.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得其中有切身利害关系，并且感到有义务彼此配合。

sentences.en: So that's another aspect of games is we're all sort of on the same playing field, right?
sentences.zh: 所以游戏的另一个方面是，我们都处在同一起跑线上，对吧？

sentences.en: In a way that we aren't at work where you may not understand the social rules or the politics.
sentences.zh: 这种方式在工作中是不存在的，在工作中你可能并不理解社交规则或办公室政治。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the game, as you pointed out just a second ago,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，正如你刚才所指出的，在游戏中，

sentences.en: we all start off on an equal footing, which actually is an important idea here.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都是从平等的起点开始的，这其实是一个很重要的概念。

sentences.en: I mean, so everyone who starts a game of chess, you know, starts with the same pieces and the same pawns.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个开始下一盘国际象棋的人，你知道的，都是从相同的棋子和兵开始的。

sentences.en: What happens then follows the rules of the game and then your creativity,
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情遵循游戏规则以及你的创造力，

sentences.en: but you're not starting out with a leg up.
sentences.zh: 但你并不是一开始就占有优势。

sentences.en: You know, someone doesn't have an extra leg up just because of who they are
sentences.zh: 不会有人仅仅因为他是谁、

sentences.en: or what school they went to or what their background or privilege might be.
sentences.zh: 或者他上过什么学校、或者他的背景或特权如何，就天然多占一点优势。

sentences.en: And that's in some ways the great democratizing aspect of games, right,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这就是游戏巨大的民主化特质，对吧，

sentences.en: is that it lets people sort of show their own ability or work, right, in sort of a pure setting.
sentences.zh: 它让人们在一个相对纯粹的环境中展现自己的能力或工作，对吧。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's why sports is appealing in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这就是为什么体育在很多方面都很有吸引力。

sentences.en: Anyone can rise up.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以崛起。

sentences.en: And that's a story we love is that somebody who, you know, unexpected becomes good
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们喜闻乐见的故事：某个出乎意料的人变得优秀了，

sentences.en: or somebody who came from an impoverished or difficult background turns out to be a champion, right?
sentences.zh: 或者某个出身贫寒或背景艰难的人最终成为了冠军，对吧？

sentences.en: And, you know, it's the same thing that happens in games as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，游戏中也会发生同样的事情。

sentences.en: One of the things I've been experimenting with is can we use games to identify extraordinary talent
sentences.zh: 我一直在试验的事情之一是：我们能否利用游戏来识别杰出的人才，

sentences.en: and find people who are, you know, have the ability to, say, be an entrepreneur
sentences.zh: 并找到那些拥有某种能力的人——比如成为企业家的能力，

sentences.en: that is unrecognized because of all those other social constraints that typically would hold us back, right?
sentences.zh: 这种能力却因为通常会阻碍我们的所有其他社会约束而被埋没，对吧？

sentences.en: Who we know, where we went to school, what resources we were born with.
sentences.zh: 我们认识谁、我们上过什么学校、我们出生时拥有什么资源。

sentences.en: And I think there's something, you know, about that game aspect
sentences.zh: 我认为游戏的这种特性，以及对游戏中人才的识别，

sentences.en: and identification of game, of talented games that is really appealing.
sentences.zh: 有某种确实非常吸引人的地方。

sentences.en: Games use a variety of psychological techniques to grab and hold our attention.
sentences.zh: 游戏利用各种心理学技巧来吸引和保持我们的注意力。

sentences.en: They encourage exploration and learning.
sentences.zh: 它们鼓励探索和学习。

sentences.en: The best games are skillfully calibrated, so we feel stimulated without feeling overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 最好的游戏都经过了巧妙的校准，让我们感到受到刺激而又不会感到不知所措。

sentences.en: Now, when non-gamers talk about games, it's often from a negative perspective.
sentences.zh: 现在，当非游戏玩家谈论游戏时，往往是从消极的角度出发。

sentences.en: Parents and educators worry about kids playing addictive or violent video games.
sentences.zh: 父母和教育工作者担心孩子们玩容易上瘾或暴力的电子游戏。

sentences.en: Managers worry that games can be a source of distraction in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 管理者担心游戏会成为工作场所的分心来源。

sentences.en: Former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg once fired a government employee for playing solitaire at work.
sentences.zh: 前纽约市长迈克尔·布隆伯格曾因一名政府雇员在工作时玩纸牌游戏而将其解雇。

sentences.en: When we come back, how some companies, organizations, and policymakers are taking a different tack.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，将探讨一些公司、组织和政策制定者如何采取不同的策略。

sentences.en: Instead of seeing games as the enemy, they are deploying what we have learned about the psychology of games
sentences.zh: 他们没有将游戏视为敌人，而是运用我们在游戏心理学中学到的知识，

sentences.en: to engage employees, entice customers, and educate citizens.
sentences.zh: 来吸引员工、招徕顾客以及教育公民。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Games rely on a range of psychological techniques to engage us and to keep us coming back for more.
sentences.zh: 游戏依赖一系列心理学技巧来吸引我们并让我们不断回头。

sentences.en: They keep score, let us roleplay, and encourage curiosity and exploration.
sentences.zh: 它们记录分数、让我们进行角色扮演，并鼓励好奇心与探索。

sentences.en: In his book, Changing the Game, and in his day job as a management researcher at the Wharton School,
sentences.zh: 在他写的书《改变游戏规则（Changing the Game）》中，以及作为沃顿商学院管理研究员的本职工作中，

sentences.en: Ethan Mollick studies how employers and policymakers are trying to incorporate features of games into the workplace
sentences.zh: 伊桑·莫里克研究了雇主和政策制定者如何试图将游戏的特色融入工作场所，

sentences.en: to promote creativity, to increase engagement, and to boost the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 以激发创造力、提高参与度并促进最终利润。

sentences.en: Ethan, research teams fighting disease often confront problems that involve mammoth amounts of very arduous work.
sentences.zh: 伊桑，抗击疾病的研究团队经常面临涉及大量极其艰巨工作的问题。

sentences.en: You talk about a computer game called Foldit that's used to come up with cures for diseases.
sentences.zh: 你提到了一个名为 Foldit 的电脑游戏，它被用来寻找疾病的治疗方法。

sentences.en: Can you explain the challenge that games like Foldit are designed to solve and how they work?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下像 Foldit 这样的游戏旨在解决什么挑战以及它们是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, Foldit represents a bunch of these really interesting games that we sometimes call citizen science.
sentences.zh: 是的，Foldit 代表了许多这种非常有趣的游戏，我们有时称之为公民科学。

sentences.en: The idea that how do we take complex tasks and outsource them to regular people, regular citizens to solve.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是：我们如何将复杂的任务剥离出来，外包给普通人、普通公民来解决。

sentences.en: And Foldit is one example of this.
sentences.zh: Foldit 就是其中的一个例子。

sentences.en: It handles a really hard problem, which is how do proteins fold?
sentences.zh: 它处理了一个非常棘手的问题，那就是蛋白质是如何折叠的？

sentences.en: So we have a sense of the sort of atomic structure of a protein,
sentences.zh: 所以我们对蛋白质的某种原子结构有了一定的了解，

sentences.en: but the shape that it takes follows all these complex rules that have never been very easy to model until quite recently on computers.
sentences.zh: 但它的形状遵循所有这些复杂的规则，直到最近在计算机上建模都不是很容易。

sentences.en: And so it's relied on scientists to try and figure out what kind of shape these proteins take,
sentences.zh: 因此，这依赖于科学家去试图弄清楚这些蛋白质呈现出什么样的形状，

sentences.en: and that determines all of their properties, what diseases they cause,
sentences.zh: 而这决定了它们所有的属性、它们引起什么疾病、

sentences.en: how they can be used to increase energy efficiency of alternative fuels, and so on.
sentences.zh: 它们如何被用来提高替代燃料的能源效率，等等。

sentences.en: And what is interesting is that people who go into, you know, cell biology or into chemistry
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那些从事细胞生物学或化学工作的人，

sentences.en: are not necessarily really great at solving three-dimensional puzzles,
sentences.zh: 不一定真的很擅长解三维谜题，

sentences.en: but there's a lot of people in the world who are really good at three-dimensional puzzles who may not know science.
sentences.zh: 但世界上有很多人非常擅长三维谜题，他们可能并不懂科学。

sentences.en: So what Foldit does is let anyone play with the structure of a protein
sentences.zh: 所以 Foldit 所做的就是让任何人都可以玩弄蛋白质的结构，

sentences.en: and fold it to try and maximize a bunch of scientific characteristics.
sentences.zh: 并将其折叠以试图使一系列科学特征最大化。

sentences.en: And what's cool is the citizens have come up with solutions that scientists struggled with.
sentences.zh: 酷炫的是，公民们想出了让科学家们绞尽脑汁的解决方案。

sentences.en: So it took people who've been working for 14 years, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，这耗费了那些一直在努力的科学家14年的时间，

sentences.en: and trying to figure out the structure of a protein in a monkey form of HIV.
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚猴子体内艾滋病毒某种蛋白质的结构。

sentences.en: And the Foldit citizen scientists were able to come up with the answer in just weeks.
sentences.zh: 而 Foldit 的公民科学家们仅用几周时间就想出了答案。

sentences.en: So there's these kind of problems that are solvable by people through games that are not solvable in other ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，存在着这样一类问题，它们可以通过游戏由人们解决，但在其他方面是无法解决的。

sentences.en: And I understand that Foldit has a collaborative component to it as well?
sentences.zh: 据我了解，Foldit 还有一个协作组件，是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the collaborative element is really interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，协作元素非常有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: We talked earlier about how we like teams and competition.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈过我们如何喜欢团队合作和竞争。

sentences.en: So actually, in Foldit, you're encouraged to join teams of people,
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，在 Foldit 中，你被鼓励加入人类团队，

sentences.en: and those teams compete against each other on a leaderboard.
sentences.zh: 这些团队在排行榜上相互竞争。

sentences.en: And the most successful teams at folding proteins are actually the teams that don't have any formal biology training.
sentences.zh: 在折叠蛋白质方面最成功的团队，实际上是那些没有任何正规生物学培训背景的团队。

sentences.en: So it's really interesting because these teams would never have been drawn to the problem if it hadn't been turned into a game.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很有趣，因为如果不是因为被变成了一个游戏，这些团队永远不会被吸引到这个问题上来。

sentences.en: But they just love solving three-dimensional puzzles.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是喜欢解三维谜题。

sentences.en: And so these street smart teams are actually beating the more scientific teams in the game.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些民间智慧团队实际上在游戏中击败了更具科学性的团队。

sentences.en: I understand that part of the reason this works is not just because some people have exceptional skills,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，这之所以有效，部分原因不仅是因为有些人拥有非凡的技能，

sentences.en: but that the elements that we've discussed earlier about gaming allow people to invest huge amounts of time in applying themselves to problems like this.
sentences.zh: 还因为我们之前讨论过的游戏元素允许人们投入大量时间来解决此类问题。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how some of these citizen science efforts are able to enlist volunteers not just to contribute their insights,
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈其中一些公民科学项目是如何招募志愿者不仅贡献他们的见解，

sentences.en: but to contribute huge amounts of time to solving problems of public interest?
sentences.zh: 而且贡献大量时间来解决公共利益问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there was another citizen science effort in a game called EVE Online,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在另一个名为《EVE Online》的游戏中也有一个公民科学项目，

sentences.en: which is sort of a giant Machiavellian spaceship simulation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种有点像巨型马基雅维利式的飞船模拟游戏。

sentences.en: You navigate the universe encased in an armored capsule deep within your ship,
sentences.zh: 你驾驶着包裹在飞船深处装甲舱内的飞船在宇宙中穿梭，

sentences.en: where you have complete neural control and function as one.
sentences.zh: 在那里你拥有完全的神经控制权并合为一体。

sentences.en: And you were able to solve problems by identifying images of cell structures and cell pathways.
sentences.zh: 你能够通过识别细胞结构和细胞通路的图像来解决问题。

sentences.en: And a total of 320,000 players identified these things over the course of a year.
sentences.zh: 在一年多的时间里，共有32万名玩家识别了这些东西。

sentences.en: They added tens of millions of images that have now made up the atlas of cell biology.
sentences.zh: 他们添加了数千万张图片，如今这些图片构成了细胞生物学图谱。

sentences.en: And the total amount of time they spent was equivalent of 72 years of researcher time to identify these characteristics.
sentences.zh: 他们花费的总时间相当于研究人员花费了 72 年的时间来识别这些特征。

sentences.en: And that's because it was built into a game that people loved and cared about.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它被内置于人们热爱和关心的游戏中。

sentences.en: And it was just integrated into their normal process.
sentences.zh: 并且它就这样被融入了他们的正常流程中。

sentences.en: I understand some companies are using games to help them build better products.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，有些公司正在利用游戏来帮助他们打造更好的产品。

sentences.en: How does Microsoft encourage employees to find bugs in critical software programs?
sentences.zh: 微软是如何鼓励员工在关键软件程序中寻找漏洞的？

sentences.en: So this is a really interesting aspect of games called gamification.
sentences.zh: 所以这是游戏一个非常有趣的面，叫做游戏化。

sentences.en: And gamification has sort of had ups and downs over the last two decades.
sentences.zh: 在过去的二十年里，游戏化经历了一些起起伏伏。

sentences.en: But the basic idea is that you're going to take elements of things that we know work in games.
sentences.zh: 但基本的想法是，你要借鉴我们在游戏中知道有效的事物的元素。

sentences.en: So those leaderboards that we talked about, competition, the idea of engagement or unlocking stories,
sentences.zh: 比如我们讨论过的那些排行榜、竞争、参与感或解锁剧情的概念，

sentences.en: and you're going to apply those aspects to work.
sentences.zh: 然后你要将这些方面应用到工作中。

sentences.en: And Microsoft has really been a leader in doing this on their own internal teaMs.
sentences.zh: 微软在他们自己的内部团队中带头做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So they have done things that have ranged from giving people badges and awards for participation,
sentences.zh: 所以他们做过各种各样的事情，从给人们颁发参与徽章和奖励，

sentences.en: which increased the number of people who are reporting bugs in their software in the internal Microsoft teams multiple times.
sentences.zh: 这使得微软内部团队中报告软件漏洞的人数增加了好几倍。

sentences.en: They've created teams that compete to find bugs or issues with software when they download it.
sentences.zh: 他们创建了团队，在下载软件时互相竞争以找出软件中的漏洞或问题。

sentences.en: And they unlock charity awards for their favorite charity.
sentences.zh: 他们为自己喜爱的慈善机构解锁慈善奖励。

sentences.en: And so there's lots of really clever techniques that they've been applying
sentences.zh: 因此，他们应用了许多非常聪明的技术

sentences.en: that have all served to increase engagement in this important bug finding,
sentences.zh: 所有这些技术都有助于提高人们对这种重要的漏洞查找活动的参与度，

sentences.en: but otherwise voluntary activity.
sentences.zh: 但这本是一项自愿的活动。

sentences.en: And it's made a huge difference in their work.
sentences.zh: 这给他们的工作带来了巨大的改变。

sentences.en: So the actual programs are being released sooner or with fewer bugs?
sentences.zh: 所以实际的程序发布得更早了，或者漏洞更少了？

sentences.en: With fewer bugs and faster.
sentences.zh: 漏洞更少，速度更快。

sentences.en: So if games can be used to encourage people to solve problems,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果游戏可以用来鼓励人们解决问题，

sentences.en: they can also be used to train people in various fields.
sentences.zh: 它们也可以用来培训各个领域的人才。

sentences.en: And one of the best examples of this might be a program called Top Gun.
sentences.zh: 其中最好的例子之一可能是一个名为《壮志凌云》的节目。

sentences.en: Ethan, can you explain the genesis of this game and how it works?
sentences.zh: 伊森，你能解释一下这个游戏的起源以及它是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: So Top Gun is actually sort of the grandfather of games.
sentences.zh: 所以《壮志凌云》实际上算是游戏的鼻祖。

sentences.en: It's actually the same Top Gun that you have seen maybe the Tom Cruise movie
sentences.zh: 它其实就是你可能看过的汤姆·克鲁斯电影里的那个《壮志凌云》

sentences.en: or the soon-to-come-out remake of the Tom Cruise movie.
sentences.zh: 或者是即将上映的汤姆·克鲁斯电影的翻拍版。

sentences.en: The end is inevitable, Maverick.
sentences.zh: 结局是不可避免的，小牛。

sentences.en: You've kind of set it for extinction.
sentences.zh: 你差不多已经让它走向灭绝了。

sentences.en: Maybe so, sir.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，长官。

sentences.en: But not today.
sentences.zh: 但不是今天。

sentences.en: And it actually is sort of one of our first indications
sentences.zh: 它实际上可以说是我们的第一批迹象之一，

sentences.en: of how important sort of games and simulations are for training.
sentences.zh: 表明游戏和模拟训练是多么重要。

sentences.en: So it actually came out of the fact that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上源于这样一个事实：美国

sentences.en: Air Force and U.S.
sentences.zh: 空军和美国

sentences.en: Navy
sentences.zh: 海军

sentences.en: had been dominant pilots in air combat from World War II up through the Korean War.
sentences.zh: 从二战到朝鲜战争一直是空战中的主导飞行员。

sentences.en: And when the Vietnam War started, suddenly American pilots were underperforming.
sentences.zh: 而当越南战争爆发时，美国飞行员的表现突然变差了。

sentences.en: So when there was a pause in the air war over Vietnam,
sentences.zh: 因此，当越南上空的空战出现间歇时，

sentences.en: both the Air Force and Navy tried to figure out how to solve this problem.
sentences.zh: 空军和海军都试图找出如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The Air Force had a lot more money, so they spent money upgrading planes,
sentences.zh: 空军有更多的资金，所以他们把钱花在升级飞机上，

sentences.en: putting new weapons in, new turning systeMs.
sentences.zh: 装上新武器、新的转向系统。

sentences.en: And the Navy, which had much less money, concentrated on a really interesting stat,
sentences.zh: 而资金少得多的海军则专注于一个非常有趣的数据，

sentences.en: which I think is really important overall,
sentences.zh: 我认为这个数据总体来说非常重要，

sentences.en: which is that the likelihood of you being shot down in air combat
sentences.zh: 那就是你在空战中被击落的可能性

sentences.en: was highest in your first mission or two.
sentences.zh: 在你的前一两次任务中是最高的。

sentences.en: If you could survive your first couple of missions, your first critical mistakes,
sentences.zh: 如果你能挺过前几次任务、前几次致命的失误，

sentences.en: you were likely to keep surviving.
sentences.zh: 你就有可能继续生存下去。

sentences.en: So they wanted to figure out how do we give people the gamified simulated experience
sentences.zh: 所以他们想弄清楚，我们如何才能给人们提供游戏化的模拟体验，

sentences.en: of getting a chance to try air combat against experts in your first couple of missions
sentences.zh: 让有机会在前几次任务中与专家进行空战较量，

sentences.en: without getting shot down in real life.
sentences.zh: 而不会在现实生活中被击落。

sentences.en: And they launched Top Gun, which is this training school in Nevada
sentences.zh: 他们推出了《壮志凌云》，这是内华达州的一个培训学校，

sentences.en: where top Navy pilots fly enemy planes against trainees.
sentences.zh: 顶尖的海军飞行员在那里驾驶敌机对抗受训人员。

sentences.en: And when the air war resumed, it was sort of like a natural experiment.
sentences.zh: 当空战恢复时，这就像是一场自然实验。

sentences.en: The Air Force continued to have worse and worse conditions in air combat,
sentences.zh: 空军在空战中的条件继续变得越来越糟，

sentences.en: but the Navy went back to being incredibly successful.
sentences.zh: 但海军又恢复了极其成功的状态。

sentences.en: So there's something about that training or practice
sentences.zh: 因此，这种训练或练习中有某种东西

sentences.en: that is really important in real life, right?
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中真的很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't want your pilot to be flying a plane for the first time with you in it.
sentences.zh: 你不会希望你的飞行员带着你第一次驾驶飞机。

sentences.en: You don't want to be the first person for a surgeon to be experimenting on.
sentences.zh: 你不会想成为外科医生拿来做实验的第一个人。

sentences.en: And games can help us get to that stage where people have real experiences
sentences.zh: 游戏可以帮助我们达到这样一个阶段：人们在真正需要拿起手术刀或驾驶飞机之前，

sentences.en: before they actually have to pick up a knife or fly a plane.
sentences.zh: 就已经有了真实的体验。

sentences.en: You mentioned the example of surgery a second ago.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了外科手术的例子。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the popular children's game called Operation,
sentences.zh: 我想到了一个名为《手术》的儿童流行游戏，

sentences.en: where you have to carefully remove various plastic organs with tweezers
sentences.zh: 你必须用镊子从一个虚构的人物身上小心翼翼地取出各种塑料器官。

sentences.en: from a make-believe character.
sentences.zh: 但我听说外科医生和医院实际上正在利用模拟和游戏

sentences.en: But I understand that surgeons and hospitals are actually using simulation and games
sentences.zh: 来真正提高进行手术的人在现实生活中的技能。

sentences.en: to actually improve the real-life skills of people performing surgeries.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 现实生活中的外科实验，对吧，玩游戏和模拟

sentences.en: Real-life surgical experiments, right, playing with games and simulations
sentences.zh: 能给你带来手术的体验，

sentences.en: that give you the experience of surgery,
sentences.zh: 现在已经成为培训医生和外科医生的关键部分。

sentences.en: is now a critical part of training doctors and surgeons.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一个模拟器教你如何与患者进行互动，

sentences.en: So, for example, there is a simulator that teaches you how to interact with patients
sentences.zh: 在其中，你首先是一个在 VR 中告诉患者某些事情的医生，

sentences.en: where you're first a doctor telling a patient something in VR
sentences.zh: 然后你可以扮演患者的角色，看着自己向他们解释事情。

sentences.en: and then you get to play the role of the patient seeing yourself explain things to them.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 所以你有点学会了病床旁的礼仪。
